outcome: Association between obstetric interventions and late preterm birth
Risk factors for late preterm birth
cohort: 917,013 infants born between 34 and 40 weeks of gestation
finding: Late preterm births had a 35% lower likelihood of obstetric interventions compared to term births, suggesting that obstetric care providers may be preferentially avoiding induction and prelabor cesarean section between 34 and 37 weeks gestation.
mod_finding: Prelabor cesarean section and induced delivery were associated with a lower likelihood of late preterm birth compared to term birth.
